blockMcqs.question: What is the primary purpose of NAT?
options: Encrypt packets between hosts
Allow many devices to share one public IP
Speed up DNS resolution
Assign IPv6 addresses automatically
blockMcqs.explanation: NAT rewrites source addresses so many private hosts appear as one public IP, conserving the scarce IPv4 address space.

blockMcqs.question: Why are private IP addresses not routable on the public internet?
options: They use a different version of TCP
Routers are configured to drop them
They have no encryption header
They conflict with DNS root servers
blockMcqs.explanation: Internet routers are configured to discard private-range packets (RFC 1918) — they are reserved for internal use only.

blockMcqs.question: How does PAT let thousands of hosts share one public IP?
options: By assigning each host a unique IPv6 address
By using different source port numbers per session
By compressing IP headers
By rotating the public IP every second
blockMcqs.explanation: PAT (NAT overload) uses unique source port numbers to distinguish sessions, so all hosts share one public IP simultaneously.

blockMcqs.question: Why is port forwarding needed with PAT?
options: PAT blocks all outbound traffic by default
PAT has no NAT table
PAT blocks unsolicited inbound connections by default
PAT only works with UDP
blockMcqs.explanation: PAT only creates table entries for outbound connections; unsolicited inbound packets have no entry to match, so they are dropped unless a forwarding rule exists.

blockMcqs.question: What key capability does a stateful firewall have that a stateless one lacks?
options: It encrypts all packets
It tracks connection state to allow reply traffic automatically
It routes packets faster than a router
It assigns IP addresses via DHCP
blockMcqs.explanation: A stateful firewall maintains a connection table; reply packets belonging to established sessions are automatically permitted without explicit rules.

blockMcqs.question: What happens when a packet matches no rule in a firewall ACL?
options: It is sent to the next router
It is held in a queue indefinitely
It is logged and re-evaluated
It is dropped by the implicit deny-all
blockMcqs.explanation: ACLs have an implicit deny-all at the bottom; unmatched traffic is silently dropped.

blockMcqs.question: What does a WAF (Web Application Firewall) inspect that an L4 firewall cannot?
options: MAC addresses
IP TTL values
HTTP payload content like SQL queries and headers
TCP window size
blockMcqs.explanation: A WAF operates at L7 and decodes HTTP, so it can inspect and block malicious payloads such as SQL injection or XSS strings.
